rationale: Every feasible run is limited by a port path at ss/max-RC with big positive slack, and T_eff tracks the target (~0.2×target + 3.9-6 ns, i.e. IO delay scales with period), so pin period_frac at 0.45. Reg-to-reg needs only ~4.2-4.4 ns. Timing-driven placement gave the fastest port paths (~3.9-4.3 vs 5.2-6.0 ns); slew-repair targets >=30% added ~70 buffers and coincided with the best ones. Both flow failures had util 38-40 (final utilisation ~1.8x setting), so pin low util and moderate density. Routing is uncongested (DRC->0): no routability spreading. Post-GRT timing repair pinned on for the tighter confirmation re-runs; synthesis, RC model, margins left free to explore.
